summary: The main article describes the use of borate esters for direct amidation and transamidation reactions. It includes two tables for optimization and substrate scope, one scheme illustrating the proposed mechanism, and a third table detailing transamidation results.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Activation of the carboxylic acid presumably occurs via in situ generation of a three or fourcoordinate boron species
items.description: This scheme illustrates the proposed mechanism for the activation of carboxylic acids by borate esters to form amides.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of Borate-Promoted Direct Carboxamidation under Microwave Conditions a
items.description: This table shows the screening of various borate reagents and solvents to optimize the microwave-assisted amidation reaction.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Borate-promoted direct amide formations
items.description: This table presents the substrate scope for the direct amidation of various carboxylic acids and amines using B(OCH2CF3)3 and B(OMe)3.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Tris(2,2,2-trifluoroethyl) borate-promoted transamidation.
items.description: This table details the conversion of primary amides to secondary amides using tris(2,2,2-trifluoroethyl) borate.
